# SEO Audit

SEO Audit for Muse is a method for auditing a Muse site the way the
2026-10-29 Skill Harbor audit was done: from the site's own data, never
from a guess about what Google might do.

It starts with Search Console performance data, in bulk, not one page at
a time: clicks, impressions and positions by query and by page, over a
stated period, with the normal Search Console lag stated honestly
(about three days). It then cross-checks with on-site navigation data:
which pages visitors actually view, which on-site searches happen, and
where the bottleneck really is. A page Google shows but nobody clicks is
a title and snippet problem. A page nobody reaches on the site either
is not a conversion problem to fix on the page itself.

It then works in order, one package at a time, and each package is
prepared only, never deployed on its own: hub titles and metas, quick
fixes (noindex on login and account pages, homepage heading, install
guide), near-miss fiches (titles and metas revised, never rewritten
blindly), language-switcher redirects, and crawled but unindexed pages.
For unindexed pages, it never rewrites titles first: it checks that
the pages are live, gives them internal links, asks for indexing one
by one in Search Console, and only then starts a new validation.

For bulk title work, it works in proposals first, never live first.
Proposals are generated for the whole catalogue, on the home PC when
possible so the main machine is not jammed, then reviewed mechanically:
